content: 1. Pesticides must not be imported, transported, or distributed unless they are packaged in a manner that ensures safety during storage, handling, and use, and does not pose unnecessary risks to human health or the environment. 2. The packaging must be resistant to degradation under normal storage and usage conditions for a specified period. 3. Pesticide packaging must not resemble common packaging used for consumable goods to avoid confusion. 4. The approved label must be prominently displayed on the packaging, providing clear instructions for use and measures to reduce risks. 5. Ideally, the packaging should include a safety mechanism to prevent children from accidentally opening the container. 6. Preferably, the packaging should be designed to make it difficult to reuse. 7. According to the Code of Conduct, packaging and repackaging of pesticides should only occur on licensed premises where staff are adequately protected from toxic hazards. 8. Governments are urged to prohibit the repackaging of pesticides into containers originally intended for food or drink. 9. Repackaging should only be allowed under strict rules, such as requiring the registration holder to perform the repackaging to ensure accountability. 10. A permit may be required for repackaging, and exceptions should only be made for damaged containers to prevent contamination, provided the new containers are labeled identically to the originals. 11. If effective controls are not feasible in a country, it may be better to prohibit repackaging entirely, except in emergencies involving leakage or high risk of leakage due to damaged packaging. 12. Pesticide legislation should prohibit packaging or repackaging without an appropriate license and ensure that all pesticides are packaged according to legal criteria. 13. Labels on pesticides must convey essential information to end users, such as how, when, and how much of the product to use, to ensure proper application and necessary precautions. 14. Labels should be in the national language(s) and include internationally recognized symbols, pictograms, and color codes where appropriate. 15. Labeling requirements should apply equally to imported and locally manufactured products. 16. Labels must include product content information, hazard and safety information, directions for use, and supplier identification with contact details. 17. Labels must be resistant to wear and tear during transport, storage, and use, and should be printed in non-fading ink and firmly affixed to the packaging. 18. If all required information cannot fit on the label, an accompanying leaflet may be included, but the label must indicate the need to read the leaflet and still include the most critical information. 19. Safety Data Sheets (SDS) should be prepared for mediumand high-risk pesticides, providing comprehensive information on ingredients, toxicology, first aid, handling, storage, and disposal. 20. SDS must comply with national requirements and, where applicable, international standards such as the Globally Harmonized System (GHS). 21. Exporting parties under the Rotterdam Convention must provide an SDS to importers for pesticides listed in Annex III or those banned or severely restricted in the exporting country. 22. Pesticide legislation should prohibit the use of pesticides for purposes or in manners not prescribed on the label and require the use of protective gear and proper application equipment. 23. Employers must provide training, protective equipment, and periodic health evaluations for workers handling pesticides to identify and address pesticide-related illnesses or injuries. 24. Employers are prohibited from recruiting children, pregnant women, or other vulnerable individuals for pesticide application that may pose unacceptable health risks. 25. Advertising of pesticides must be regulated to prevent false or misleading claims and ensure compliance with registration and labeling requirements. 26. Legislation should prohibit the advertising of unregistered or illegal pesticides and ensure that all advertising statements are technically justified and not misleading. 27. National authorities should monitor and enforce advertising standards, with penalties for violations, to ensure responsible promotion of pesticide products.
